summary: Built the shared foundation layer for the uc123 module on the Python/FastAPI/PostgreSQL stack CLAUDE.md specifies (TASK.md's own verification steps referenced `dotnet`, which does not apply here -- CLAUDE.md wins on HOW per the task's own precedence rule). Added SQLAlchemy ORM entities for all 10 contract tables with mixins for the shared audit/soft-delete columns, one hand-written Alembic migration per required name in the exact required order (verified via alembic's offline --sql rendering: correct Postgres types, FKs and indexes end to end), migrations-at-startup wiring in app/main.py's lifespan hook, a centralized error layer (404/409/400/500 all resolving to the one {error, details} body), and paging primitives (PageParams/PagedResponse) for later `is_paged` endpoints. Also found and fixed a real bug in the pre-existing app/auth.py: both X-User-Role/X-User-Id APIKeyHeader dependencies lacked an explicit scheme_name, so FastAPI collapsed them into one OpenAPI security scheme and only one header was ever documented -- exactly the Swagger-UI failure CLAUDE.md calls out. Added 20 passing tests (health, auth 401/403/200, centralized error shapes, pagination, and ORM-metadata-vs-contract equivalence). `python -m compileall app` and `pytest -q` both pass; the health route was verified live against a running uvicorn instance. No business endpoints were added, per scope.

code_files.description: SQLAlchemy engine/session wiring; Base is None-safe when DATABASE_URL is unset so importing models never requires a live database.
NotFoundError/ConflictError/ValidationFailedError -- shared HTTPException subclasses resource tasks raise to get 404/409/400 through the one error body.
Modified: added a lifespan hook that runs `alembic upgrade head` at startup (no-op without DATABASE_URL), a catch-all Exception handler for 500, and details passthrough on the shared error body.

Modified: gave each APIKeyHeader dependency an explicit, distinct scheme_name so X-User-Role and X-User-Id both appear in the OpenAPI security schemes instead of colliding on the same auto-generated name.
Package marker for app/schemas.
PageParams (page/pageSize/search/sortBy/sortOrder query binding) and a generic PagedResponse for endpoints marked is_paged.
TimestampMixin (created_at/created_by/updated_at/updated_by) and SoftDeleteMixin (deleted_at/deleted_by) shared by every entity.
Tenant ORM entity for the `tenants` table.
User ORM entity for the `users` table, with idx_users_tenant_role.
Counterparty ORM entity for the `counterparties` table, with idx_counterparties_tenant_gst.
UploadedFile ORM entity for the `uploaded_files` table.
Template and TemplateVersion ORM entities for `templates` and `template_versions`.
Clause and ClauseVersion ORM entities for `clauses` and `clause_versions`.
Contract and ContractTask ORM entities for `contracts` and `contract_tasks`, with all three contract indexes.
Imports every entity so Base.metadata is fully populated for Alembic and for tests.
Alembic configuration; sqlalchemy.url is deliberately left unset here and wired in at runtime from DATABASE_URL.
Alembic environment: reads DATABASE_URL via app.config.settings, imports app.models so target_metadata is complete.
Alembic revision template.
CreateTenants -- creates the `tenants` table.
CreateUsers -- creates the `users` table with FK to tenants and idx_users_tenant_role.
CreateCounterparties -- creates the `counterparties` table with FK to tenants and idx_counterparties_tenant_gst.
CreateUploadedFiles -- creates the `uploaded_files` table with FK to tenants.
CreateTemplates -- creates the `templates` table with FK to tenants and idx_templates_tenant_type_industry_status.
CreateTemplateVersions -- creates the `template_versions` table with FKs to templates and users.
CreateClauses -- creates the `clauses` table with FK to tenants and idx_clauses_tenant_status.
CreateClauseVersions -- creates the `clause_versions` table with FKs to clauses and users.
CreateContracts -- creates the `contracts` table with FKs to tenants/templates/uploaded_files/counterparties/users and its three indexes.
CreateContractTasks -- creates the `contract_tasks` table with FKs to contracts/users and idx_contract_tasks_assignee_current.
Shared TestClient fixture.
Health route returns 200.
401 on missing role header, 403 on disallowed/unknown role, 200 on a permitted role; regression test that X-User-Role and X-User-Id are declared as distinct OpenAPI security schemes.
404/409/400/500 all resolve to the shared {error, details} body, including an unhandled exception and a framework RequestValidationError.
PageParams defaults, overrides, and sortOrder validation.

Every context.json table/column/index is mirrored exactly by Base.metadata; the migration chain resolves to the exact required order; the full upgrade renders as valid offline SQL without a live database.

pr.title: feat(uc123): foundation -- persistence layer, migrations, auth/error/paging infra
pr.body: Implements T-00-FOUNDATION-API: SQLAlchemy entities for all 10 uc123 tables, one Alembic migration per required name in the exact required order, migrations-applied-at-startup wiring, a centralized error-handling layer (404/409/400/500 -> one shared body), paging primitives for `is_paged` endpoints, and a fix to a real header-auth/OpenAPI bug in app/auth.py. No business endpoints implemented, per scope -- see blockers for judgement calls and the one verification gap (no reachable Postgres in this sandbox).

blockers: Could not verify 'migrations apply cleanly against a fresh database' against a live PostgreSQL instance: this sandbox has no reachable Postgres (connection to localhost:5432 refused) and Bash is restricted to ls/mkdir/kill/curl/python/python3/pip/pytest/uvicorn/alembic/ruff, so I could not start one (docker run, apt-get, pg_isready, service postgresql all require approval and were not available). Mitigated by: (1) running the full upgrade chain through alembic's offline `--sql` mode, which renders every CREATE TABLE/INDEX statement without a live connection -- manually reviewed and matches context.json's types, nullability, FKs and indexes exactly for all 10 tables; (2) an automated test (tests/test_persistence.py) asserting the ORM metadata matches context.json table-for-table, column-for-column, index-for-index, and that the migration chain resolves to the exact required order; (3) booting the actual app with uvicorn and confirming /health and the shared error body work live (DATABASE_URL unset, so migration startup is a documented no-op in that mode). A real Postgres run is still recommended before this is trusted in production.

TASK.md's own verification steps (`dotnet build Api.sln`, `dotnet test Api.sln`, `dotnet run --project src/Api`) assume a .NET stack. This repo's CLAUDE.md specifies Python/FastAPI/PostgreSQL, and the task instructions say CLAUDE.md wins on HOW. I substituted CLAUDE.md's own checks instead: `python -m compileall app` and `pytest -q` (20/20 passing), plus `uvicorn app.main:app --port 5199` for the live health-route check.

IDs are generated at the app layer (SQLAlchemy column default=uuid.uuid4 in app/models/mixins.py and each entity's `id` column) rather than via a Postgres server default such as gen_random_uuid(). Both are explicitly permitted by CLAUDE.md ('a database default ... or the app layer at insert time'); I chose the app layer so no pgcrypto/uuid-ossp extension needs to be enabled as a migration side effect. Any resource task that inserts rows via raw SQL bypassing the ORM must supply an id explicitly.

Found and fixed a pre-existing bug in app/auth.py (not introduced by this task but squarely inside the shared auth infrastructure this task owns): both the X-User-Role and X-User-Id APIKeyHeader() instances lacked an explicit `scheme_name`, so FastAPI's OpenAPI generation collapsed them to the same auto-derived component name ('APIKeyHeader') and only one header ended up declared in the generated docs -- the exact Swagger 'Authorize' failure CLAUDE.md calls out by name. Fixed by setting distinct `scheme_name` values and added tests/test_auth.py::test_openapi_declares_both_auth_headers_as_distinct_security_schemes as a regression guard.

Added app/errors.py (NotFoundError/ConflictError/ValidationFailedError) as the minimum shared exception vocabulary resource tasks need to hit 404/409/400 through the one error body -- context.json does not enumerate an exception hierarchy, so this was derived directly from CLAUDE.md's 'Status codes' and 'Errors use ONE shared body' sections, not invented business logic.

No business endpoints, services, or repositories were implemented -- out of scope per TASK.md ('You do NOT implement any business endpoint'). The only runtime route is the existing /health check; a handful of routes defined inline inside pytest test modules (tests/test_auth.py, tests/test_errors.py, tests/test_pagination.py) exist solely to exercise the shared auth/error/paging infrastructure end-to-end through TestClient and are never registered outside the test process.
